transcript.display:
### Understanding your situation
You are a tenant who vacated a flat in Pune on 15 August 2026 and handed over the keys. Your landlord is withholding your ₹40,000 security deposit without giving any reason, despite there being no damage and no pending rent.

### Where you stand legally
- Your landlord is required to refund the security deposit at the time of taking over vacant possession, after making due deductions for any liability, if the state has enacted a law based on the Model Tenancy Act. [1]
- At the end of the lease, you are required to hand back possession of the property to the landlord. [2]
- You have a general limitation period of three years from when the right to sue accrues to file a civil suit to recover money such as an unreturned security deposit. [3]

### Your options
1. **Civil Suit for Money Recovery** — File a civil suit in the appropriate civil court to recover the ₹40,000 security deposit based on the three-year limitation period. [3]

### Time limits
- You have a limitation period of three years from when the right to sue accrues to file a civil suit for recovering the unreturned security deposit. [3]

### What to do next
1. Send a written demand to your landlord asking for the return of your ₹40,000 security deposit.
2. Organize your rent agreement and bank transfer proof of the deposit.
3. Consult a local advocate in Pune to discuss filing a civil money recovery suit if the landlord continues to withhold the amount.

### Keep these ready
- Rent agreement
- Bank transfer proof of the deposit
- Any written communication with the landlord regarding the handover of keys and the deposit

### Draft: Legal notice (edit before using)
> To,
> [Landlord's Name]
> [Landlord's Address]
>
> Subject: Demand for refund of security deposit of ₹40,000
>
> Dear Sir/Madam,
>
> I was a tenant at your property in Pune under our rent agreement. I vacated the flat and handed over the keys to you on 15 August 2026.
>
> There was no damage to the property and no rent pending at the time of vacating. You have withheld my security deposit of ₹40,000 without providing any reason.
>
> I request you to kindly refund the amount of ₹40,000 to my bank account within [Number] days of receiving this notice.
>
> Sincerely,
> [Your Name]
> [Your Contact Information]

### When to involve a lawyer
- You can usually start this yourself. If the other side does not respond, or you are unsure about any step, consult a lawyer.
- Free legal aid: NALSA helpline **15100**, or your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA).

### Assumptions and gaps
- The Model Tenancy Act provisions depend on whether Maharashtra has enacted a law based on it; otherwise, the state's rent law and your rent agreement govern the deposit.
- It is assumed there are no other written clauses in your rent agreement that alter the standard deposit refund terms.

---
**Sources (Bare Act provisions)**
1. Section 11, *Model Tenancy Act, 2021* — Security deposit limits and refund
2. Section 108, *Transfer of Property Act, 1882* — Rights and duties of landlord and tenant
3. Article 113 (Schedule), *Limitation Act, 1963* — General limitation period for civil money suits
